item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q009_heme_bundle_fold_not_homology","answer":"No. SCOPe 2.08 places them in three separate superfamilies within fold f.21, “Heme-binding four-helical bundle” (sunid 81344): transmembrane di-heme cytochromes, f.21.1 (81342); fumarate reductase respiratory complex transmembrane subunits, f.21.2 (81343); and respiratory nitrate reductase 1 gamma chain, f.21.3 (103501). The fold belongs to class f, “Membrane and cell surface proteins and peptides” (56835).\n\nTheir shared fold describes structural similarity; it does not establish common ancestry across these superfamilies. Superfamily membership supports probable common ancestry, whereas families are more closely related groups within superfamilies. These three groups are not merely different families of one homologous superfamily. Their separation does not prove that an ancient evolutionary relationship is impossible, but SCOPe does not assert one. Shared heme binding and bundle architecture alone cannot justify transferring specific respiratory functions, substrate specificity, or detailed mechanistic annotations. A structure from one group may inform a broad architectural comparison, but is not automatically a valid homology-modeling template or functional representative for the others; such uses require independent sequence/profile, detailed structural, and biochemical evidence.","evidence_used":["/api/v1/","/api/v1/releases/2.08/search?q=heme","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/81344","/api/v1/releases/2.08/search?q=f.21","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/56835","/api/v1/releases/2.08/resolve/f.21.2","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/81342"]}]}
